αἰγύπτου: Αἴγυπτος — Egypt, the river/land; fem. gen. sg. (Αἰγύπτου προπάροιθε ’off the coast of Egypt’)
βάλλουσιν: βάλλω — throw, cast; here of launching ships into the sea; pres. 3 pl.
βίη: βίη — might, bodily strength, force; fem. nom. sg.
βίης: βίη — might, force; fem. gen. sg., gen. of separation with σχέσθαι ’hold back from force’
βοσκομένη: βόσκω — feed, pasture; mid. graze; pres. part. mid. fem. nom. sg. (of the hind grazing)
βούλοντο: βούλομαι — wish, will, be minded; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἐβούλοντο): ’they wished’
βροτῷ: βροτός — mortal; masc. dat. sg., agreeing with ἀνδρί: ’to/for a mortal man’
γέροντος: γέρων — old man, elder; masc. gen. sg. (ἁλίοιο γέροντος ’of the old man of the sea’, θείοιο/τοῖο γέροντος ’of the divine/that old man’, epithets of Proteus)
γίγνονται: γίγνομαι — become, come into being; pres. 3 pl.: ’they come to be’ (of creatures that exist upon earth)
γαλαθηνοὺς: γαλαθηνός — milk-fed, suckling, still at the breast; epic compound adj., masc. acc. pl.
γαστέρα: γαστήρ — belly, stomach; fem. acc. sg.
γιγνόμενος: γίγνομαι — become; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’becoming, turning into’ (of Proteus’s shape-shifting)
γλαφυροῖσιν: γλαφυρός — hollow; masc./neut. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οῖς): ’in the hollow caves’ (σπέσσι γλαφυροῖσιν)
γλαφυρὴ: γλαφυρός — hollow; fem. nom. sg. (γλαφυρὴ νηῦς ’a hollow ship’, of a ship’s rounded hull)
γναμπτοῖς: γναμπτός — bent, curved; verbal adj. of γνάμπτω ’bend’; masc. dat. pl., agreeing with ἀγκίστροισιν: ’with bent hooks’
γουνούμενος: γουνόομαι — supplicate, entreat (lit. clasp by the knees, γόνυ); pres. part. mid. masc. nom. sg.
δήθ: δηθά (elided δήθ’) — for long, long since; adv., intensified by δή: ’for so long now’
δολιχὴν: δολιχός — long; adj., fem. acc. sg., agreeing with ὁδόν: ’a long (journey)’
δύναιο: δύναμαι — be able, can; pres. opt. 2 sg. mid.: ’you might be able, if you could’ (εἴ πως ... δύναιο, potential condition)
δύνασαι: δύναμαι — be able, can; pres. 2 sg. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic δύνασαι/δύνῃ): ’you can, you are able’
εἰδοθέη: Εἰδοθέη — Eidothea, a sea-nymph, daughter of Proteus, who helps Menelaus; fem. nom. sg. (first appearance in the poem)
εἰρωτᾷς: εἰρωτάω (epic = ἐρωτάω) — ask, question; pres. 2 sg.
εἰσήλυθεν: εἰσέρχομαι — go/come into, enter; epic aor. 3 sg. εἰσήλυθεν (= Attic εἰσῆλθεν): ’he came into’
εἴποιμι: εἶπον (aor. of λέγω/φημί) — say, tell; aor. opt. 1 sg., potential with ἄν: ’I would say’
εἴπῃσιν: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσιν (ν-movable, = Attic εἴπῃ)
εἴρεσθαι: εἴρομαι (= ἔρομαι) — ask, inquire; aor. inf. mid., used as an imperative: ’(and) ask!’
εὐνάσω: εὐνάζω — lay to bed, lay down to rest; fut. 1 sg. act.: ’I will lay (you) down’
εὐνηθῆναι: εὐνάω — lay in bed; aor. pass. inf. εὐνηθῆναι, used in a middle sense: ’to lie (in bed)’
εὐρυπόροιο: εὐρύπορος — wide-wayed, with wide paths (εὐρύς + πόρος); adj., fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
εὑρέμεναι: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. inf. act., epic -έμεναι (= Attic εὑρεῖν)
ζεφύροιο: Ζέφυρος — the West Wind, personified; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θεσπιδαὲς: θεσπιδαής — wondrously blazing (θέσπις + δαίω ’burn’); adj., neut. nom./acc. sg., epithet of fire
καλυφθείς: καλύπτω — cover, hide; aor. pass. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’covered, veiled’
καλῆς: καλός — beautiful, fair; fem. gen. sg.
κατέφθιτο: καταφθίνω (root φθίω/φθίνω) — perish, be destroyed utterly; aor. mid. 3 sg., with κε in an unreal past condition: ’would have perished’
κατερύκομαι: κατερύκω — hold back, detain; pres. pass. 1 sg.: ’I am held back, detained’
κατευνηθέντα: κατευνάω — lull, lay to rest; aor. pass. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’laid down to rest, asleep’ (of Proteus)
κείνοισιν: κεῖνος (= Attic ἐκεῖνος) — that, yonder; demonstr. pron./adj., masc. dat. pl.: ’upon those men’
κεχάροντο: χαίρω — rejoice, be glad; redupl. aor. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’they rejoiced’
κικλήσκουσι: κικλήσκω (= καλέω) — call, name; pres. 3 pl., ν lost before enclitic: ’they call (it)’
κιόντι: κίω — go, walk; pres. part. masc. dat. sg., agreeing with μοι: ’as (I) went’
κνημοὺς: κνημός — mountain slope, spur, ridge; masc. acc. pl.
κοιμήθημεν: κοιμάω — put to sleep; pass. lie down to rest; aor. pass. 1 pl.: ’we lay down to sleep’
κοιμήσασα: κοιμάω — lull to sleep, put to rest; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg.: ’having lulled to rest’
κοιμᾶται: κοιμάω — mid. lie down to rest, sleep; pres. 3 sg. mid.: ’he lies down to sleep’
κρίνασθαι: κρίνω — pick out, choose, select; aor. inf. mid., used as an imperative: ’choose!’
κρατεροῖο: κρατερός — strong, mighty; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
κρατερόφρονος: κρατερόφρων — strong-minded, stout of heart (κρατερός + φρήν); adj., masc. gen. sg.
κρατερῶς: κρατερῶς — mightily, forcefully; adv. from κρατερός
κυμαίνοντα: κυμαίνω — swell, billow (of the sea, from κῦμα ’wave’); pres. part. masc. acc. sg., agreeing with πόντον: ’billowing, surging’
λέξεται: λέχομαι (root λεχ-, distinct from λέγω ’say, gather’) — lie down to rest; fut. mid. 3 sg.: ’he will lie down’
λίσσεαι: λίσσομαι — beg, entreat, beseech; pres. 2 sg. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic λίσσῃ)
λελαβέσθαι: λαμβάνω — take, seize, catch; perf. inf. mid. (reduplicated), stressing a firm grip: ’to get hold of, catch fast’
λιμός: λιμός — hunger, famine; masc. nom. sg.
λιμὴν: λιμήν — harbor, haven; masc. nom. sg.
λοχησάμενος: λοχάω — lie in ambush, lie in wait; aor. part. mid. masc. nom. sg.: ’having lain in ambush’
λῦσαί: λύω — loose, release, let go; aor. inf. act., used as an imperative: ’release!, let go!’
μάλιστά: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα, accented μάλιστά before a following enclitic (γε): ’most of all, especially’
μέλλω: μέλλω — be about to, be likely to; pres. 1 sg. + inf., expressing a supposition: ’I must be...’
μένε: μένος — might, vigor, strength; neut. acc. pl. μένεα, elided μένε(’) before a vowel: ’the men’s strength’ (κατέφθιτο ... μένε’ ἀνδρῶν)
μέσσῃσι: μέσος (epic μέσσος) — middle, in the midst; fem. dat. pl. μέσσῃσι used substantively: ’among them, in their midst’ (of Proteus among the seals)
μήλων: μῆλον — sheep, small cattle; neut. gen. pl.
μεθίεις: μεθίημι — let go, relax; mid. sense here, relax one’s effort, give up; pres. 2 sg. act.: ’you give up, you slacken’
μεμαῶτα: μέμονα — be eager, be minded, strive; perf. part. (pres. sense) masc. acc. sg. μεμαώς, μεμαῶτα: ’eager, straining’
μεμνῆσθαι: μιμνήσκω — remind; mid./pass. remember, be mindful; perf. inf. mid., pres. force: ’to be mindful’ + gen.
μινύθει: μινύθω — lessen, waste away, dwindle; pres. 3 sg. intrans.: ’wastes away’
μᾶλλόν: μάλα — very; comparative adv. μᾶλλον ’more, rather’, accented μᾶλλόν before the enclitic τε: ’all the harder’
νέποδες: νέποδες — offspring, brood; masc./fem. nom. pl., used only of these seals in Homer, ’children (of Halosydne)’; formation and precise meaning disputed
νήπιός: νήπιος — foolish, childish, witless; adj., masc. nom. sg., accented νήπιός before the enclitic εἰς
νεβροὺς: νεβρός — fawn, young deer; masc./fem. acc. pl.
νεηγενέας: νεηγενής — newborn, newly-born (νέος + γίγνομαι); epic compound adj., masc./fem. acc. pl.
νημερτής: νημερτής — unerring, infallible, truthful (νη- + ἁμαρτάνω); adj., masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Proteus (γέρων ἅλιος νημερτής)
νημερτὴς: νημερτής — unerring, infallible, truthful; adj., masc. nom. sg., running-text (grave) accent, standing epithet of Proteus
νηῶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. pl., epic νηῶν (= Attic νεῶν)
νομεὺς: νομεύς — herdsman, shepherd; masc. nom. sg.
ξυλόχῳ: ξύλοχος — thicket, copse, lair; masc. dat. sg.
οἴῳ: οἶος — alone, only; adj., masc. dat. sg., agreeing with an implied dat. of the speaker: ’alone’
οἷός: οἷος — such as, of what sort; relative adj., masc. nom. sg., correlative with τοῖος: ’such as, as ... when’
οὐδέν: οὐδείς, οὐδεμία, οὐδέν — no one, nothing; neut. acc. sg.: ’nothing, no (word)’
οὖροι: οὖρος — a fair, favouring wind; masc. nom. pl.
πάσας: πᾶς — all, every; fem. acc. pl., substantival: ’all of them’ (the seals)
πάσχων: πάσχω — suffer, experience; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’suffering’
πανημερίη: πανημέριος — all day long, the whole day; adj., fem. nom. sg. used adverbially with νηῦς ἤνυσεν: ’in a whole day’s sailing’
παρακλιδόν: παρακλιδόν — aslant, evasively, swerving from the truth; rare adv.
παρὲξ: παρέξ — beside, past, beyond; adv./prep. + acc., here adverbial with εἴποιμι: ’say otherwise, speak beside the point’
πεδάᾳ: πεδάω — fetter, shackle, hold fast; pres. ind. 3 sg., epic uncontracted
πειρήσεται: πειράω — try, test, make trial of; fut. mid. 3 sg.
πεμπάσσεται: πεμπάζομαι — count by fives (from πέμπε, old form of πέντε); aor. subj. 3 sg. mid., after ἐπήν in a generalizing temporal clause: ’when he has counted them’
πεποίθεα: πείθω — persuade; mid./pass. trust, rely on; plpf. 1 sg. (impf./perf. force): ’I had come to trust, I trusted’ + dat.
πιέζειν: πιέζω — press, squeeze hard, grip; pres. inf. act., used as an imperative: ’press hard, grip!’
πνείοντες: πνέω — blow, breathe; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., agreeing with οὖροι: ’blowing’
πνοιῇ: πνοιή — breath, blast, breeze; fem. dat. sg.
ποιήεντα: ποιήεις — grassy; adj., neut. acc. pl., epithet of ἄγκεα ’glens’
πολυβενθέος: πολυβενθής — very deep, many-fathomed (πολύς + βένθος); adj., fem. gen. sg.
πολυκλύστῳ: πολύκλυστος — much-dashed-by-waves, much-surging (κλύζω ’surge, wash over’); adj., masc. dat. sg.
προδαεὶς: προδαείς (προ- + δαῆναι ’learn’) — having learned beforehand, having got wind of; aor. pass. part. masc. nom. sg.
προσέειπον: προσεῖπον (aor. of πρόσφημι) — speak to, address; aor. 1 sg.
προϊδὼν: προοράω — see beforehand, foresee; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.
πρωτέος: Πρωτεύς — Proteus, the shape-shifting old man of the sea; masc. gen. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic Πρωτέως)
πρωτεὺς: Πρωτεύς — Proteus, the shape-shifting old man of the sea, servant of Poseidon; masc. nom. sg.
πωλεῖταί: πωλέομαι — come and go regularly, frequent; pres. 3 sg. mid., iterative force: ’he comes here regularly’
πόρφυρε: πορφύρω — heave, seethe, churn (properly of the sea darkening/heaving); impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, applied metaphorically to a troubled heart
πώεσι: πῶυ — flock (esp. of sheep); neut. dat. pl., epic -εσι
πώς: πώς (= enclitic πως) — somehow, in any way; accented πώς because followed by a further enclitic (με): ’lest he somehow...’
πᾶσαν: πᾶς — all, every; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with ἰθύν: ’for every (undertaking)’
στᾶσα: ἵστημι — stand, set; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg. (root aor. ἔστην): ’having stood, standing’
συνήντετο: συναντάω — meet, come upon; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented, + dat.: ’she met (me)’
σχέσθαι: ἔχω — have, hold; mid. σχέσθαι, restrain oneself, hold back; aor. inf. mid., used as an imperative, + gen. of separation: ’hold back (your force)!’
τέκμωρ: τέκμωρ — a fixed mark, sign, end, limit; neut. nom./acc. sg. (indecl.), of an escape not found
τέρπεαι: τέρπω — mid. delight in, take pleasure; pres. 2 sg. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic τέρπῃ)
τέτυκται: τεύχω — make, build; pass. come to pass, happen; perf. pass. 3 sg.: ’has been made, has come to pass’
τεκέσθαι: τίκτω — bring forth, beget; aor. inf. mid., of the father’s part in begetting (the act. is used of the mother’s bearing): ’to have begotten’
τεληέσσας: τεληείς — complete, fulfilling, perfect (of sacrifice, from τέλος); adj., fem. acc. pl.
τῆμος: τῆμος — then, at that time; correlative temporal adv. answering ἦμος ’when’
φάρον: Φάρος — Pharos, an island off Egypt; acc. sg., proper name, first appearance in the poem
φαίνονθ: φαίνω — show; mid./pass. appear; impf. 3 pl. mid., elided φαίνονθ’ (= ἐφαίνοντο), unaugmented: ’they appeared’
φαινομένηφιν: φαίνομαι — appear, show oneself; pres. part. (dat. sg. sense) φαινομένηφιν, the rare -φι(ν) suffix, elsewhere confined to nouns, attached here unusually to a participle: ’(Dawn) as she appears’ — a genuinely rare formation
φιλομηλεΐδῃ: Φιλομηλεΐδης — Philomeleides, a legendary king of Lesbos known only from this wrestling-story; masc. dat. sg.
φράζευ: φράζω — mid. think out, devise, plan; pres. imper. 2 sg. mid., epic -ευ (= Attic -ου): ’devise! plan!’
φρικὶ: φρίξ — ripple, roughening of the sea’s surface; fem. dat. sg.
φώκας: φώκη — seal (the sea-animal); fem. acc. pl.
φώνησέν: φωνέω — utter, speak aloud, call out; aor. 3 sg., accented φώνησέν before the enclitic τε
φῶκαι: φώκη — seal (the sea-animal); fem. nom. pl.
χαλέπτει: χαλέπτω — be harsh to, afflict, vex (from χαλεπός); pres. 3 sg.
χαλίφρων: χαλίφρων — slack-minded, foolish (χαλάω ’slacken’ + φρήν); adj., masc. nom. sg., rare compound
ψαμάθοισιν: ψάμαθος — sand; fem. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀγαγοῦσα: ἄγω — lead, bring; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg.
ἀγκίστροισιν: ἄγκιστρον — fish-hook; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀθανάτους: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. acc. pl., substantival: ’the immortals’
ἀλέηται: ἀλέομαι — avoid, escape, shun; aor. subj. mid. 3 sg., after μή in a clause of fearing: ’lest he escape’
ἀλιτέσθαι: ἀλιταίνω — sin against, transgress against, offend; aor. inf. mid., with μέλλω: ’to be offending’
ἀλύξαι: ἀλύσκω — flee, escape, avoid; aor. inf. act., epexegetic: ’to escape’ (of Proteus straining to get away)
ἀλώμενοι: ἀλάομαι — wander, roam; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.
ἀμβροσίη: ἀμβρόσιος — ambrosial, divine, immortal; adj., fem. nom. sg., standing epithet of night
ἀμείβετο: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented
ἀμφιβεβήκῃ: ἀμφιβαίνω — stride astride, bestride; perf. subj. 3 sg., in a generalizing temporal clause: ’has reached (the zenith)’
ἀμφοτέροισι: ἀμφότερος — both (of two); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀνάλκιδες: ἄναλκις — without might, strengthless, feeble (ἀ- + ἀλκή); adj., masc. nom. pl., predicate
ἀναστάς: ἀνίστημι — raise up; intrans. aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg. ἀναστάς: ’having risen up, rising’
ἀνείρηται: ἀνείρομαι (= ἔρομαι) — ask, question, inquire of; aor. subj. mid. 3 sg.
ἀποπνείουσαι: ἀποπνέω — breathe out, exhale; pres. part. act. fem. nom. pl.
ἀργαλέην: ἀργαλέος — hard, grievous, painful; fem. acc. sg.
ἀργαλέος: ἀργαλέος — hard, difficult, grievous; adj., masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’(a god is) hard (for a mortal to master)’
ἀστεμφέως: ἀστεμφέως — unyieldingly, unflinchingly, without wavering; adv.
ἀφυσσάμενοι: ἀφύσσω — draw (water or wine); aor. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.: ’having drawn (for themselves)’
ἁθρόαι: ἁθρόος — crowded together, in a mass, all together; adj., fem. nom. pl.
ἁλίοιο: ἅλιος — of the sea, belonging to the sea; adj., masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), epithet of γέρων ’the old man of the sea’
ἁλιαέες: ἁλιαής — blowing off the sea, sea-borne (of winds); adj., masc. nom. pl., rare compound found only here in Homer
ἁλοσύδνης: Ἁλοσύδνη — Halosydne, an epithet-name for a sea-goddess (usually identified with Amphitrite), whose formation and exact meaning are uncertain; fem. gen. sg., kept as a proper name
ἄγκεα: ἄγκος — glen, valley, mountain-hollow; neut. acc. pl.
ἄγον: ἄγω — lead, bring, take along; impf. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγον): ’I took along’
ἄνευθ: ἄνευθε(ν) (elided ἄνευθ’) — far off, apart, away; adv.
ἅλιος: ἅλιος — of the sea, belonging to the sea; adj., masc. nom. sg., part of the standing epithet γέρων ἅλιος νημερτής ’the old man of the sea’ (of Proteus)
ἐδύσετο: δύω/δύνω — enter, sink into, plunge; aor. mid. 3 sg., epic sigmatic (ἐδύσετο, = Attic ἔδυ): ’she plunged (in)’
ἐλεύσεαι: ἔρχομαι (fut. ἐλεύσομαι) — go, come; fut. mid. 2 sg., epic uncontracted: ’you shall come’ (the fixed νόστον formula)
ἐλεύσομαι: ἔρχομαι (fut. ἐλεύσομαι) — go, come; fut. mid. 1 sg., epic uncontracted: ’I shall come’
ἐξαναδῦσαι: ἐξαναδύω — rise up out of, emerge from; aor. part. act. fem. nom. pl.
ἐξερέῃσι: ἐξερέομαι — search out, range over, explore; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσι, generalizing with ὁπότε (no ἄν/κε needed): ’ranges over’
ἐπάλαισεν: παλαίω — wrestle; aor. 3 sg., + dat. of the opponent: ’he wrestled (against)’
ἐπί: ἐπί — on, upon, towards; here as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἐπί ... ἤλυθεν = ἐπῆλθεν ’came on, came upon’); accented ἐπί before the following enclitic τε
ἐπικεύσω: ἐπικεύθω — hide further, keep back, conceal in addition; fut. 1 sg.
ἐπιπνείῃσιν: ἐπιπνέω — blow upon, blow after; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσιν, generalizing (parallel to ἐξερέῃσι): ’blows (behind it)’
ἐρύκεαι: ἐρύκω — hold back, restrain, detain; pass. be held back; pres. 2 sg. pass., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἐρύκῃ)
ἐσάωσε: σαόω (= σῴζω) — save, preserve; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’saved’
ἐσσύμενόν: σεύω — set in motion, drive; mid./pass. perf. part. ἐσσύμενος, rush, be eager, strain; masc. acc. sg., accented before the enclitic περ: ’straining hard, eager’
ἐυκτιμένῃ: ἐυκτίμενος — well-built, well-founded (ἐύ + κτίζω); adj., fem. dat. sg., epithet here of an island
ἐυσσέλμοισιν: ἐύσσελμος — well-benched (σέλμα ’rowing-bench, deck-beam’); adj., fem. dat. pl., epic -οισιν, epithet of ships
ἐφάμην: φημί — say, speak; impf. mid. 1 sg., epic uncontracted: ’I was speaking, I spoke’
ἐφήσει: ἐφίημι — send/let loose upon, launch at; fut. 3 sg.
ἐφετμέων: ἐφετμή — command, injunction, behest; fem. gen. pl., rare epic noun
ἐφῆκεν: ἐφίημι — send/let loose upon; aor. 3 sg., augmented
ἐχέμεν: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. inf. act., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἔχειν), used as an imperative: ’hold on!’
ἐύορμος: ἐύορμος — with good anchorage, well-mooring (ὅρμος ’anchorage’); adj., masc. nom. sg.
ἐών: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic ἐών (= Attic ὤν), accented ἐών before a pause: ’being’ (τοῖος ἐών ’being such’)
ἑρπετὰ: ἑρπετόν — creeping thing; broadly, any living creature, not narrowly reptiles; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἑὴν: ἑός (= ὅς, ἥ, ὅν possessive) — his own, her own; 3rd-person reflexive possessive adj., fem. acc. sg. ἑήν, agreeing with εὐνήν: ’his own (lair)’
ἔβαλε: βάλλω — throw, cast, throw down; aor. 3 sg., here in tmesis with κατά (κὰδ δ’ ἔβαλε = κατέβαλε): ’threw down’
ἔδησε: δέω — bind, tie; aor. 3 sg., + gen. of separation: ’has bound (me) away from’
ἔλαφος: ἔλαφος — deer, hind; fem. nom. sg.
ἔπεισιν: ἔπειμι (εἶμι + ἐπί) — go over, go among, inspect; pres. 3 sg., used with future sense alongside ἀριθμήσει: ’(will) go among (them), inspect’
ἔρεξα: ῥέζω — do, perform; esp. offer sacrifice; aor. 1 sg.
ἔριδος: ἔρις — strife, quarrel, contention; fem. gen. sg.
ἔρροντι: ἔρρω — wander, roam (elsewhere often ’go to ruin, go wretchedly’); pres. part. dat. sg., agreeing with μοι (elided μ’): ’as I wandered’
ἔτειρε: τείρω — wear away, distress, afflict; impf. 3 sg., augmented
ἠοῖ: ἠώς — dawn; fem. dat. sg. ἠοῖ
ἤθελον: ἐθέλω — be willing, wish; impf. 3 pl., augmented: ’they wished’
ἤματ: ἦμαρ — day; neut. acc. pl. ἤματα, elided ἤματ’ before a vowel: ’(for) days’
ἤνυσεν: ἀνύω — accomplish, achieve, complete (a distance/journey); aor. 3 sg.
ἰθύν: ἰθύς (noun) — a direct course, an undertaking, a purpose; fem. acc. sg., distinct from the homographic adverb ἰθύς ’straight’
ἰφθίμου: ἴφθιμος — stout, strong, mighty; adj., masc. gen. sg.
ἰχθυάασκον: ἰχθυάω — fish (denom. of ἰχθύς); impf. iterative 1 pl., epic -ασκ- suffix marking repeated action: ’we used to fish, we kept fishing’
ἴδησθε: εἶδον (aor. of ὁράω) — see; aor. subj. mid. 2 pl., in a generalizing temporal clause: ’when you see’
ἴδηται: εἶδον (aor. of ὁράω) — see; aor. subj. mid. 3 sg., in a generalizing temporal clause: ’when he looks (them) over’
ὀδμήν: ὀδμή — smell, odor; fem. acc. sg.
ὀλοφύρατο: ὀλοφύρομαι — lament, pity, feel compassion for; aor. 3 sg. mid.
ὀλοφώια: ὀλοφώιος — baneful, harmful, deceitful (formation disputed, perhaps connected with ὄλλυμι ’destroy’); adj. used substantively, neut. acc. pl.: ’baneful arts/wiles’
ὁπλισάμεσθ: ὁπλίζω — make ready, prepare, equip; aor. mid. 1 pl., elided ὁπλισάμεσθ’ (= ὁπλισάμεσθα): ’we got (supper) ready’
ὁπότ: ὁπότε (elided ὁπότ’) — when, whenever; temporal conj., here introducing a vivid simile
ὄρινα: ὀρίνω — stir, move, arouse (the heart, emotions); aor. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ὤρινα): ’I moved, stirred’
ὅθ: ὅθι (elided ὅθ’) — where; relative adv. of place (distinct from ὅτε ’when’, similarly elided ὅτ’)
ὅσσον: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος) — as much/great as; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, correlative with τόσσον: ’as far as’
ὑποδμώς: ὑποδμώς — an underling, a subject slave (ὑπό + δμώς ’slave’); masc. nom. sg., a startling word applied here to Proteus as subordinate to Poseidon
ᾗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. dat. sg.: ’for which, to which’ (referring back to the ship, νηῦς)
ῥηγμῖνι: ῥηγμίς — the line of breaking surf, the beach at the waterline (ῥήγνυμι ’break’); fem. dat. sg.

__broaden__.αἰγύπτιος: Αἰγύπτιος — Aegyptius, an elder of Ithaca; masc. nom. sg. · also used as an adjective, ’Egyptian, of Egypt’, epithet of Proteus (ἀθάνατος Πρωτεὺς Αἰγύπτιος); masc. nom. sg.
__broaden__.αἰγύπτῳ: Αἴγυπτος — Egypt; fem. dat. sg., poetic dat. of direction: ‘to Egypt’ · also a plain dative of place where, ’in Egypt’ (Αἰγύπτῳ ... ἔσχον ’the gods held me back in Egypt’)
__broaden__.εὐνήν: εὐνή — bed, bedding, marriage-bed; fem. acc. sg. · also of an animal’s lair, den (ἑὴν εἰσήλυθεν εὐνήν ’came into his own lair’, of the lion in the simile)
__broaden__.δαμῆναι: δαμάζω — subdue, overpower; aor. pass. inf.: ‘to be overcome’ (of death or fate) · also used of overpowering a god by main force (θεὸς ... δαμῆναι ’a god is hard to subdue’), not only of death or fate
__broaden__.μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
__broaden__.μελαίνῃ: μέλας — black; standing epithet of ships; fem. dat. sg. μέλαινα · also modifying a different noun, not a ship (μελαίνῃ φρικί ’with a dark ripple’, of the sea’s surface)
__broaden__.κατήλυθον: κατέρχομαι — come down, put in (from the sea); aor. 1 sg. · also aor. 3 pl. (identical form): ’they came down’ (of Telemachus and Athena reaching the ship) · also aor. 1 pl.: ’we came down’ (forced by the following verb)
__broaden__.κακόν: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. sg.: ’a bad thing, evil’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal passive (κακόν τ’ ἀγαθόν τε τέτυκται ’whatever, good or bad, has come to pass’)
__broaden__.ἀγαθόν: ἀγαθός — good; neut. acc. sg.: ’good, a good thing’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal passive (κακόν τ’ ἀγαθόν τε τέτυκται ’whatever, good or bad, has come to pass’)
__broaden__.κὰδ: κατά (apocope κάδ before δ-) — down through, throughout; prep./preverb in tmesis: ’throughout the halls’ (κὰδ δώματα = κατὰ δώματα) · also a bare preverb in tmesis with a verb: κὰδ ... ἔβαλε = κατέβαλε ’threw down’
__broaden__.κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’
__broaden__.τρεῖς: τρεῖς — three; numeral, masc./fem. nom. pl. · also masc./fem. acc. pl. (same syncretic form): ’three’ (ἑταίρους τρεῖς ’three companions’, acc.)
__broaden__.ἔχειν: ἔχω — have, hold, keep; pres. inf. · also used as an imperative, a regular Homeric idiom for commands: ’hold (him) fast!’ (αὖθι δ’ ἔχειν μεμαῶτα)
__broaden__.ἤια: ἤια — provisions for a journey; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl. (subject): ’our stores’ · also a different word, impf. 1 sg. of εἶμι ’go’: ’I was going’, unrelated to this noun
__broaden__.ἥρως: ἥρως — hero, man of standing; masc. nom. sg. · also used as a vocative in direct address, inserted mid-sentence (ἥρως, εἴρεσθαι δέ ’and ask, hero that you are’), distinct from its use as a narrative title ’the hero’
__broaden__.ἰχθυόεντα: ἰχθυόεις — fish-filled, teeming with fish; neut. acc. pl. (ἰχθυόεντα κέλευθα ’fish-filled paths’, of the sea) · also masc. acc. sg. w/ πόντον: ’upon the fish-teeming sea’, not only neut. acc. pl. of κέλευθα
__broaden__.οἷσι: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν — his own, her own; possessive adj. (distinct from the relative ὅς); masc. dat. pl.: ’his own’ · also the relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (not the possessive): ’in whom’ (ἑταίρους ... οἷσι μάλιστα πεποίθεα)
__broaden__.ὅσσ: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος, double σ) — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl., elided (ὅσσ’ = ὅσσα): ’as much as’ · also neut. nom. pl., subject of a verb: ὅσσ’ ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἑρπετὰ γίγνονται ’as many creatures as come to be upon earth’
